title: Pre-nuptial agreements - are they enforceable in India
p1:
Can a couple decide their financial future before marriage?

Many people assume a pre-nuptial agreement can completely protect their assets in India, just like it does in some other countries. But the reality is more complicated.
p2: In India, pre-nuptial agreements are not automatically recognised as legally binding contracts in the same way they are in many Western jurisdictions. Personal laws, public policy considerations, and the nature of marriage as a legal relationship can affect their enforceability.
p3:
However, that does not mean such agreements have no value. They can still record the intentions of both partners, clarify financial arrangements, and serve as evidence of mutual understanding if disputes arise. The key is ensuring the agreement is fair, voluntary, and not against existing laws.

A well-drafted agreement may not guarantee a court outcome, but it can help avoid confusion and future conflicts.
conclusion: Should Indian couples have the option to legally enforce pre-nuptial agreements before marriage? Share your view.
